title_en: Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted in accordance with the Constitution, reflecting the experience and actual circumstances of civil trial work in China.

Article 2 The objectives of this Law are to protect the exercise of litigation rights by parties, ensure that the People's Courts ascertain facts, distinguish right from wrong, correctly apply the law, promptly adjudicate civil cases, confirm civil rights and obligations relationships, impose sanctions on civil illegal acts, protect the lawful rights and interests of parties, educate citizens to voluntarily abide by the law, uphold social and economic order, and guarantee the smooth progress of socialist construction.

Article 3 The provisions of this Law shall apply to civil actions initiated between citizens, between legal persons, between other organizations, and among them, concerning property relations and personal relations, which are accepted by the People's Courts.
Article 4 All persons conducting civil actions within the territory of the People's Republic of China must abide by this Law.

Article 5 Foreigners, stateless persons, foreign enterprises and organizations initiating or responding to lawsuits in the People's Courts shall enjoy equal litigation rights and obligations as Chinese citizens, legal persons and other organizations.
Where a foreign court imposes restrictions on the civil action rights of Chinese citizens, legal persons and other organizations, the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China shall apply the principle of reciprocity to the civil action rights of the citizens, enterprises and organizations of that country.

Article 6 The adjudicative power over civil cases shall be exercised by the People's Courts.
The People's Courts shall independently adjudicate civil cases in accordance with the provisions of law, and shall not be subject to interference by administrative organs, social organizations or individuals.
Article 7 When adjudicating civil cases, the People's Courts must take facts as the basis and the law as the criterion.

Article 8 Parties to civil actions shall have equal litigation rights. When adjudicating civil cases, the People's Courts shall safeguard and facilitate the exercise of litigation rights by the parties, and shall apply the law equally to all parties.
Article 9 When adjudicating civil cases, the People's Courts shall conduct mediation on the basis of voluntariness and legality; if mediation fails, they shall render a judgment in a timely manner.

Article 10 When adjudicating civil cases, the People's Courts shall, in accordance with the provisions of law, implement the systems of collegial panels, withdrawal, open trial, and final instance of two trials.

Article 11 Citizens of all ethnic groups shall have the right to conduct civil actions in their own spoken and written languages.
In areas inhabited by minority ethnic groups or where multiple ethnic groups live together, the People's Courts shall conduct adjudication and issue legal instruments in the commonly used spoken and written languages of the local ethnic groups.
The People's Courts shall provide translation for litigation participants who do not understand the commonly used spoken and written languages of the local ethnic groups.
Article 12 When the People's Courts adjudicate civil cases, the parties shall have the right to argue.

Article 13 Civil actions shall adhere to the principle of good faith.
Parties shall have the right to dispose of their own civil rights and litigation rights within the scope provided for by law.
Article 14 The People's Procuratorates shall have the authority to exercise legal supervision over civil actions.

Article 15 Organs, social organizations, enterprises and institutions may support the injured unit or individual in initiating a lawsuit in the People's Court against acts that damage the civil rights and interests of the State, a collective or an individual.

Article 16 With the consent of the parties, civil action activities may be conducted online through information network platforms.
Civil action activities conducted online through information network platforms shall have the same legal effect as offline litigation activities.

Article 17 The People's Congresses of national autonomous areas may, in accordance with the principles of the Constitution and this Law, and taking into account the specific circumstances of the local ethnic groups, formulate flexible or supplementary provisions. Provisions of autonomous regions shall be submitted to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for approval. Provisions of autonomous prefectures and autonomous counties shall be submitted to the Standing Committee of the People's Congress of the province or autonomous region for approval and shall be reported to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for the record.
Article 18 Primary People's Courts shall have jurisdiction over first instance civil cases, except as otherwise provided by this Law.
Article 20 Higher People's Courts shall have jurisdiction over first instance civil cases that have a significant impact within their respective jurisdictions.

Article 22 A civil action against a citizen shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place of the defendant's domicile; if the defendant's domicile is inconsistent with the place of habitual residence, the action shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place of habitual residence.
A civil action against a legal person or other organization shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place of the defendant's domicile.
If the places of domicile or habitual residence of several defendants in the same action fall within the jurisdictional areas of two or more People's Courts, each of those People's Courts shall have jurisdiction.
Article 24 An action arising from a contract dispute shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place of the defendant's domicile or at the place of performance of the contract.

Article 25 An action arising from an insurance contract dispute shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place of the defendant's domicile or at the location of the subject matter of the insurance.

Article 26 An action arising from a negotiable instrument dispute shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place of payment of the instrument or at the place of the defendant's domicile.

Article 27 An action arising from a dispute over the establishment of a company, confirmation of shareholder qualification, distribution of profits, dissolution, or the like, shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place of the company's domicile.

Article 28 An action arising from a dispute over a contract for railway, road, water, air or combined transportation shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place of departure, the place of destination, or the place of the defendant's domicile.
Article 29 An action arising from a tort shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place where the tort was committed or at the place of the defendant's domicile.

Article 30 An action seeking damages arising from a railway, road, water or air accident shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place where the accident occurred, or at the place where the vehicle or vessel first arrived, or where the aircraft first landed, or at the place of the defendant's domicile.

Article 31 An action seeking damages arising from a collision of ships or other maritime damage incidents shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place where the collision occurred, or at the place where the colliding ship first arrived, or at the place where the offending ship was detained, or at the place of the defendant's domicile.

Article 32 An action arising from salvage fees at sea shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place where the salvage took place or at the place where the salved ship first arrived.

Article 33 An action arising from general average shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place where the ship first arrived, or at the place where the general average adjustment was conducted, or at the place where the voyage ended.

Article 35 Parties to a dispute over a contract or other property rights and interests may, by written agreement, select the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place of the defendant's domicile, the place of performance of the contract, the place of conclusion of the contract, the place of the plaintiff's domicile, the place where the subject matter is located, or any other place that has a substantial connection with the dispute; however, this shall not violate the provisions of this Law concerning hierarchy jurisdiction and exclusive jurisdiction.

Article 36 In an action over which two or more People's Courts have jurisdiction, the plaintiff may initiate the lawsuit in any one of those People's Courts; if the plaintiff initiates the lawsuit in two or more of those People's Courts that have jurisdiction, the People's Court that first places the case on file shall have jurisdiction.

Article 37 If a People's Court discovers that a case it has accepted does not fall within its jurisdiction, it shall transfer the case to the People's Court that has jurisdiction, and the transferee People's Court shall accept the case. If the transferee People's Court considers that the transferred case does not fall within its jurisdiction according to the provisions, it shall submit a report to the superior People's Court for designation of jurisdiction and may not further transfer the case on its own.

Article 38 If a People's Court that has jurisdiction is unable to exercise its jurisdiction due to special reasons, the superior People's Court shall designate another court to have jurisdiction.
If a dispute over jurisdiction arises between People's Courts, the disputing parties shall resolve it through consultation; if consultation fails, they shall submit a report to their common superior People's Court for designation of jurisdiction.

Article 39 A superior People's Court shall have the authority to adjudicate first instance civil cases under the jurisdiction of a lower People's Court; if it is truly necessary to transfer a first instance civil case under its own jurisdiction to a lower People's Court for adjudication, it shall submit a report to its superior People's Court for approval.
If a lower People's Court considers that a first instance civil case under its jurisdiction needs to be adjudicated by a superior People's Court, it may submit a report to the superior People's Court for adjudication.

Article 40 When adjudicating first instance civil cases, the People's Courts shall form a collegial panel composed of judges and people's assessors jointly, or a collegial panel composed of judges alone. The number of members in a collegial panel shall be odd.
Civil cases adjudicated using the summary procedure shall be tried by a single judge alone. First instance civil cases adjudicated by a Primary People's Court with clear basic facts and well-defined rights and obligations relationships may be tried by a single judge alone applying the ordinary procedure.
When participating in adjudicative activities, people's assessors shall have equal rights and obligations as judges, except as otherwise provided by law.

Article 41 When a People's Court tries a civil case of second instance, it shall form a collegial panel composed of judges. The number of members of a collegial panel shall be an odd number.
For a civil case of second instance that was concluded by the Intermediate People's Court in first instance using summary procedure or upon an appeal against a ruling, where the facts are clear and the rights and obligations are definite, with the consent of both parties, the case may be tried by a single judge alone.
For a case remanded for retrial, the original trial People's Court shall form a collegial panel separately in accordance with the procedure of first instance.
For a case tried on retrial, if it was originally tried in first instance, a collegial panel shall be formed separately in accordance with the procedure of first instance; if it was originally tried in second instance or if it is brought up for trial by a superior People's Court, a collegial panel shall be formed separately in accordance with the procedure of second instance.

Article 43 Where a People's Court, in the course of trial, finds that a case is not suitable for trial by a single judge alone, it shall rule to transfer the case to a collegial panel for trial.
If a party considers that trial of a case by a single judge alone violates legal provisions, it may raise an objection to the People's Court. The People's Court shall examine the objection raised by the party; if the objection is established, it shall rule to transfer the case to a collegial panel for trial; if the objection is not established, it shall rule to reject the objection.

Article 44 The presiding judge of a collegial panel shall be designated by the president or the division chief from among the judges; if the president or the division chief participates in the trial, he or she shall serve as the presiding judge.

Article 45 When a collegial panel deliberates on a case, the principle of the minority being subordinate to the majority shall apply. A record of the deliberation shall be made and signed by the members of the collegial panel. Different opinions expressed during the deliberation shall be truthfully recorded in the record.

Article 46 Adjudicators shall handle cases impartially in accordance with law.
Adjudicators shall not accept any treat or gifts from parties or their litigation agents.
If an adjudicator commits acts of corruption, bribery, favoritism, or rendering a judgment contrary to law, legal liability shall be pursued; if such acts constitute a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated in accordance with law.

Article 47 An adjudicator shall withdraw himself or herself under any of the following circumstances, and the parties shall have the right to apply for his or her withdrawal orally or in writing:
(1) He or she is a close relative of a party or a litigation agent in the case;
(2) He or she has an interest in the case; or
(3) He or she has another relationship with a party or a litigation agent in the case that may affect the impartial trial of the case.
If an adjudicator accepts treats or gifts from a party or a litigation agent, or meets with a party or a litigation agent in violation of regulations, the party shall have the right to request his or her withdrawal.
If an adjudicator commits acts as provided in the preceding paragraph, legal liability shall be pursued in accordance with law.
The provisions of the preceding three paragraphs shall apply to judge assistants, court clerks, judicial technical personnel, interpreters, expert witnesses, and inspectors.

Article 48 A party applying for withdrawal shall state the reasons and shall make the application at the commencement of the trial; if the grounds for withdrawal become known after the commencement of the trial, the application may also be made before the conclusion of the court debate.
The person whose withdrawal is applied for shall suspend participation in the work of the case pending a decision by the People's Court on whether to grant the withdrawal, except in cases where the case requires urgent measures.

Article 49 Withdrawal of the president of the court when he or she serves as the presiding judge or as a sole judge shall be decided by the judicial committee; withdrawal of an adjudicator shall be decided by the president; withdrawal of other personnel shall be decided by the presiding judge or the sole judge.

Article 50 A People's Court shall, within three days after the application for withdrawal is made, render a decision orally or in writing. If the applicant is dissatisfied with the decision, he or she may apply for one reconsideration at the time of receiving the decision. During the period of reconsideration, the person whose withdrawal is applied for shall not cease participation in the work of the case. The People's Court shall, within three days, render a reconsideration decision and notify the person applying for reconsideration.

Article 51 Citizens, legal persons, and other organizations may serve as parties in a civil action.
A legal person shall conduct litigation through its legal representative. Other organizations shall conduct litigation through their principal responsible persons.

Article 52 A party shall have the right to appoint an agent, apply for withdrawal, collect and provide evidence, engage in debate, request mediation, file an appeal, and apply for enforcement.
A party may consult the relevant materials of the case and may reproduce the relevant materials and legal documents of the case. The scope and methods for consulting and reproducing the relevant materials of the case shall be specified by the Supreme People's Court.
A party must exercise litigation rights in accordance with law, observe the litigation order, and perform legally effective judgments, rulings, and mediation documents.
Article 53 The parties may reach a settlement between themselves.
Article 54 The plaintiff may waive or modify his or her claims. The defendant may admit or rebut the claims and shall have the right to file a counterclaim.

Article 55 Where one party or both parties consist of two or more persons, and the object of action is the same, or the object of action is of the same category and the People's Court considers that the cases may be tried jointly and the parties consent, it shall be a joint action.
If a party to a joint action has joint rights and obligations in respect of the object of action, the litigation act of one of them shall be effective for the other joint litigants only if it is admitted by the other joint litigants; if a party has no joint rights or obligations in respect of the object of action, the litigation act of one of them shall not be effective for the other joint litigants.

Article 56 For a joint action in which a large number of persons on one party are involved, the parties may elect representatives to conduct the litigation. The litigation acts of the representatives shall be effective for the parties they represent; however, if the representatives modify or waive claims, admit the claims of the opposing party, or settle the case, they must obtain the consent of the parties they represent.

Article 57 Where the object of action is of the same category, one party consists of a large number of persons, and the exact number of persons is unknown at the time of filing the action, the People's Court may issue a public notice, explaining the case situation and the claims, and notifying the right holders to register with the People's Court within a specified period.
The right holders who have registered with the People's Court may elect representatives to conduct the litigation; if no representatives are elected, the People's Court may appoint representatives in consultation with the registered right holders.
The litigation acts of the representatives shall be effective for the parties they represent; however, if the representatives modify or waive claims, admit the claims of the opposing party, or settle the case, they must obtain the consent of the parties they represent.
The judgments and rulings made by the People's Court shall be effective for all the right holders who have registered. If a right holder who has not registered files an action within the limitation of action, such judgment or ruling shall apply.

Article 58 For acts that damage the public interest, such as polluting the environment or infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of a large number of consumers, the authorities and relevant organizations as provided by law may institute an action in a People's Court.
Where a People's Procuratorate, in the course of performing its duties, discovers acts that damage the public interest, such as damaging the ecological environment and resource protection, or infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of a large number of consumers in the fields of food and drug safety, it may institute an action in a People's Court, provided that there is no authority or organization as provided in the preceding paragraph, or if such authority or organization fails to institute an action. If the authority or organization provided in the preceding paragraph institutes an action, the People's Procuratorate may support the action.

Article 59 If a third party considers that it has an independent claim to the object of action of both parties, it shall have the right to institute an action.
If a third party does not have an independent claim to the object of action of both parties, but the outcome of the case has a legal interest in relation to it, it may apply to participate in the proceedings, or the People's Court shall notify it to participate. If a People's Court renders a judgment holding a third party liable for civil liability, such third party shall have the litigation rights and obligations of a party.
If a third party as provided in the preceding two paragraphs fails to participate in the proceedings for reasons not attributable to itself, but has evidence proving that part or all of the legally effective judgment, ruling, or mediation document is erroneous and damages its civil rights and interests, it may, within six months from the date it becomes aware or should have become aware of the damage to its civil rights and interests, institute an action before the People's Court that rendered such judgment, ruling, or mediation document. If, after trial, the claims are established, the People's Court shall modify or revoke the original judgment, ruling, or mediation document; if the claims are not established, it shall dismiss the claims.

Article 60 A person without capacity for litigation shall have his or her guardian act as legal agent to conduct litigation on his or her behalf. If the legal agents shift their responsibility to each other, the People's Court shall designate one of them to conduct the litigation.

Article 61 A party or legal agent may appoint one or two persons as litigation agents.
The following persons may be appointed as litigation agents:
(1) Lawyers and basic-level legal service workers;
(2) Near relatives or staff members of the party; and
(3) Citizens recommended by the community, unit, or relevant social organization to which the party belongs.

Article 62 To appoint another person to conduct litigation on its behalf, a party must submit a power of attorney signed or sealed by the appointing party to the People's Court.
The power of attorney must clearly specify the matters entrusted and the scope of authority. For a litigation agent to admit, waive, or modify claims, reach a settlement, file a counterclaim, or file an appeal, the appointing party must provide special authorization.
A power of attorney sent or delivered from abroad by a citizen of the People's Republic of China residing abroad must be certified by the embassy or consulate of the People's Republic of China in that country; if there is no such embassy or consulate, it shall be certified by the embassy or consulate of a third country that has diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China in that country, and then further certified by the embassy or consulate of the People's Republic of China in that third country, or certified by a local patriotic overseas Chinese organization.
Article 63 If the authority of a litigation agent is modified or revoked, the party shall inform the People's Court in writing, and the People's Court shall notify the opposing party.

Article 64 Lawyers and other litigation agents representing a party in litigation shall have the right to investigate and collect evidence and may consult the relevant materials of the case. The scope and methods for consulting the relevant materials of the case shall be specified by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 65 In a divorce case where a litigation agent is appointed, the party personally shall still appear in court, unless he or she is unable to express his or her will; if the party is truly unable to appear in court due to special circumstances, he or she must submit a written opinion to the People's Court.

Article 67 A party shall have the responsibility to provide evidence for its own claims.
If evidence that a party or its litigation agent cannot collect on its own due to objective reasons, or evidence that the People's Court considers necessary for trial, the People's Court shall investigate and collect it.
The People's Court shall examine and verify evidence comprehensively and objectively in accordance with legal procedures.

Article 68 A party shall provide evidence for its own claims in a timely manner.
The People's Court shall, based on the claims of the parties and the circumstances of the case, determine the evidence that the parties shall provide and the time limit therefor. If a party truly has difficulty providing evidence within such time limit, it may apply to the People's Court for an extension, and the People's Court shall appropriately extend the time limit based on the party's application. If a party provides evidence beyond the time limit, the People's Court shall order it to state the reasons; if it refuses to state the reasons or the reasons are not established, the People's Court may, depending on the circumstances, either refuse to admit the evidence, or admit the evidence but impose a reprimand or fine.

Article 69 Upon receiving evidence materials submitted by a party, the People's Court shall issue a receipt specifying the names, number of pages, number of copies, whether they are originals or copies, and the time of receipt, among other things, and the receipt shall be signed or sealed by the handling personnel.

Article 70 A People's Court shall have the authority to investigate and collect evidence from relevant units and individuals, and such units and individuals shall not refuse.
The People's Court shall distinguish the authenticity of certifying documents submitted by relevant units and individuals and shall examine and determine their validity.

Article 71 Evidence shall be presented in court and subject to cross-examination by the parties. Evidence involving state secrets, trade secrets, or personal privacy shall be kept confidential; if it needs to be presented in court, it shall not be presented during an open hearing.

Article 72 Legal facts and documents that have been notarized through legal procedures shall be used by the People's Court as a basis for finding facts, unless there is evidence to the contrary sufficient to overturn the notarized proof.

Article 73 Documentary evidence shall be submitted in its original form. Physical evidence shall be submitted in its original form. If it is truly difficult to submit the original form, reproductions, photographs, copies, or extracts may be submitted.
If documentary evidence in a foreign language is submitted, a Chinese translation must be attached.

Article 74 A People's Court shall distinguish the authenticity of audio-visual materials and, in conjunction with other evidence in the case, examine and determine whether they may be used as a basis for finding facts.

Article 75 Any unit or individual that knows the circumstances of a case shall have the obligation to testify in court. The responsible persons of relevant units shall support witnesses in testifying.
A person who cannot correctly express his or her will may not testify.

Article 77 The necessary expenses, including transportation, accommodation, and meals, as well as the loss of wages, incurred by a witness in fulfilling the obligation to testify in court shall be borne by the losing party. If a party applies for a witness to testify, that party shall advance the payment; if no party applies and the People's Court notifies a witness to testify, the People's Court shall advance the payment.

Article 78 A People's Court shall, in conjunction with other evidence in the case, examine and determine whether a party's statements may be used as a basis for finding facts.
A party's refusal to make statements shall not affect the People's Court's determination of the case facts based on evidence.

Article 79 A party may apply to the People's Court for an expert evaluation on a specialized issue for the purpose of ascertaining the facts. If a party applies for an expert evaluation, the parties shall consult to determine a qualified expert evaluator; if consultation fails, the People's Court shall designate an expert evaluator.
If a party does not apply for an expert evaluation, and the People's Court considers that an expert evaluation is necessary for a specialized issue, it shall entrust a qualified expert evaluator to conduct the evaluation.

Article 80 An expert evaluator shall have the right to access the case materials necessary for the evaluation and may, when necessary, question the parties or witnesses.
The expert evaluator shall submit a written expert opinion and sign or seal the evaluation report.

Article 81 If a party disagrees with an expert opinion or a People's Court considers it necessary for an expert to appear in court, the expert shall testify in court. Where an expert, after being notified by the People's Court, refuses to testify in court, the expert opinion shall not be used as the basis for ascertaining facts; and the party that has paid the appraisal fees may request the return of the appraisal fees.

Article 82 A party may apply to the People's Court to notify a person with specialized knowledge to appear in court and give opinions on the expert opinion made by the expert or on specialized issues.

Article 83 In examining physical evidence or the scene, the inspector must show the credentials of the People's Court and invite local grassroots organizations or the unit to which a party belongs to send persons to participate. A party or his/her adult family member shall be present; if they refuse to be present, such refusal shall not affect the progress of the inspection.
The relevant entities and individuals shall, pursuant to the notification of the People's Court, have the obligation to preserve the scene and assist in the inspection.
The inspector shall make a record of the inspection status and results, which shall be signed or sealed by the inspector, the party, and the invited participants.

Article 84 Where evidence may be lost or become difficult to obtain later, a party may, during the litigation, apply to the People's Court for preservation of evidence, and the People's Court may also take preservation measures on its own motion.
In urgent circumstances, where evidence may be lost or become difficult to obtain later, an interested party may, before filing a lawsuit or applying for arbitration, apply to the People's Court at the place where the evidence is located, the domicile of the respondent, or the People's Court having jurisdiction over the case for preservation of evidence.
For other procedures for the preservation of evidence, refer to the relevant provisions on preservation in Chapter IX of this Law.

Article 85 Time periods include statutory time periods and time periods designated by the People's Court.
Time periods shall be calculated by hours, days, months, and years. The hour and day from which a time period begins shall not be counted within the time period.
If the last day of a time period falls on a statutory holiday, the day following the statutory holiday shall be deemed as the expiration date of the time period.
Time periods shall not include time in transit; if litigation documents are posted before the expiration date, they shall not be deemed as overdue.

Article 86 Where a party misses a deadline due to force majeure or other justifiable reasons, he/she may, within ten days after the obstacle is removed, apply for an extension of the time period, and whether to grant such extension shall be decided by the People's Court.

Article 87 Service of litigation documents must be accompanied by a service receipt, on which the recipient shall record the date of receipt and sign or affix his/her seal.
The date of signing by the recipient on the service receipt shall be the date of service.

Article 88 Service of litigation documents shall be made directly to the recipient. If the recipient is a citizen, and he/she is not present, the documents may be served on his/her adult family member living with him/her for signature; if the recipient is a legal person or any other organization, the documents shall be served on the legal representative of the legal person, the principal of such other organization, or the person responsible for receiving documents in such legal person or organization for signature; if the recipient has a litigation agent, the documents may be served on such agent for signature; if the recipient has designated a person to receive documents to the People's Court, the documents shall be served on such designated person for signature.
The date of signature on the service receipt by the adult family member living with the recipient, the person responsible for receiving documents in the legal person or other organization, the litigation agent, or the designated recipient shall be the date of service.

Article 89 Where the recipient or his/her adult family member living with him/her refuses to accept litigation documents, the server may invite representatives from the relevant grassroots organization or the recipient's work unit to be present, explain the situation, record on the service receipt the reasons for refusal and the date, have the server and witnesses sign or affix their seals, and leave the litigation documents at the recipient's domicile; alternatively, the server may leave the litigation documents at the recipient's domicile and record the service process by means such as taking photos or videos, and the documents shall be deemed as served.

Article 90 With the consent of the recipient, a People's Court may serve litigation documents by electronic means capable of confirming receipt by the recipient. Where judgments, rulings, or mediation documents are served by electronic means, and the recipient requests paper documents, the People's Court shall provide them.
Where service is effected by the method in the preceding paragraph, the date on which the service information reaches the recipient's specified system shall be the date of service.

Article 91 Where direct service of litigation documents is difficult, service may be entrusted to another People's Court, or service may be made by mail. For service by mail, the date of receipt noted on the return receipt shall be the date of service.
Article 92 Where the recipient is a military serviceman, the documents shall be forwarded through the political department of the unit at or above the regimental level to which he/she belongs.

Article 93 Where the recipient is imprisoned, the documents shall be forwarded through the prison where he/she is held.
Where the recipient is subjected to compulsory educational measures, the documents shall be forwarded through the compulsory educational institution where he/she is held.

Article 94 After receiving litigation documents, the authorities or entities that forward them must immediately deliver them to the recipient for signing, and the date of signature on the service receipt shall be the date of service.

Article 95 Where the recipient's whereabouts are unknown, or service cannot be effected by other methods provided in this Section, service shall be made by public announcement. Service shall be deemed to have been completed thirty days after the date the announcement is published.
For service by public announcement, the reasons and process shall be recorded in the case file.

Article 96 When a People's Court hears civil cases, it shall conduct mediation based on the principle of voluntariness of the parties, on the basis of clear facts, and after distinguishing right from wrong.

Article 97 Mediation by a People's Court may be presided over by a single judge or by a collegial panel, and shall, to the extent possible, be conducted at the location.
When a People's Court conducts mediation, it may notify parties and witnesses to appear in court by simple means.

Article 98 When a People's Court conducts mediation, it may invite relevant entities and individuals to assist. The invited entities and individuals shall assist the People's Court in conducting mediation.
Article 99 For a mediation agreement to be reached, both parties must do so voluntarily, and no party shall be coerced. The content of the mediation agreement shall not violate the provisions of law.

Article 100 Where a mediation agreement is reached, the People's Court shall prepare a mediation document. The mediation document shall state the claims, the facts of the case, and the result of the mediation.
The mediation document shall be signed by the judge and the court clerk, affixed with the seal of the People's Court, and served on both parties.
The mediation document shall have legal effect after it is signed by both parties.
Article 102 Where a mediation agreement is not reached or a party retracts before the mediation document is served, the People's Court shall render a judgment in a timely manner.

Article 103 For cases where, due to the conduct of one party or other reasons, it may become difficult to enforce a judgment or cause other damage to a party, the People's Court may, upon the application of the other party, rule to preserve the party's property, order him/her to perform a certain act, or prohibit him/her from performing a certain act; if the party does not apply, the People's Court may, when necessary, also rule to take preservation measures.
When taking preservation measures, the People's Court may order the applicant to provide security; if the applicant fails to provide security, the court shall rule to dismiss the application.
After accepting an application, if there is an emergency, the People's Court must make a ruling within forty-eight hours; if the court rules to take preservation measures, the measures shall be implemented immediately.

Article 104 Where, due to an emergency, failure to apply for preservation immediately would cause irreparable damage to the legitimate rights and interests of an interested party, the party may, before filing a lawsuit or applying for arbitration, apply to the People's Court at the place where the property to be preserved is located, the domicile of the respondent, or the People's Court having jurisdiction over the case for preservation measures. The applicant shall provide security; if the applicant fails to provide security, the court shall rule to dismiss the application.
After accepting an application, the People's Court must make a ruling within forty-eight hours; if the court rules to take preservation measures, the measures shall be implemented immediately.
If the applicant fails to file a lawsuit or apply for arbitration in accordance with the law within thirty days after the People's Court takes preservation measures, the People's Court shall lift the preservation.
Article 105 Preservation shall be limited to the scope of the request or to the property relevant to the case.

Article 106 Property preservation is effected by sealing up, distraining, freezing, or other methods as provided by law. After preserving property, the People's Court shall immediately notify the person whose property is preserved.
Any property that has been sealed up or frozen shall not be sealed up or frozen again.
Article 107 In property dispute cases, if the respondent provides security, the People's Court shall rule to lift the preservation.
Article 108 If an application is erroneous, the applicant shall compensate the respondent for any losses suffered as a result of the preservation.

Article 110 For a People's Court to rule to grant advance execution, the following conditions shall be met:
(1) the rights and obligations between the parties are clear, and failure to grant advance execution would seriously affect the applicant's livelihood or production and business operations;
(2) the respondent has the ability to perform.
The People's Court may order the applicant to provide security; if the applicant fails to provide security, the court shall dismiss the application. If the applicant loses the case, he/she shall compensate the respondent for any property losses suffered as a result of the advance execution.

Article 111 If a party disagrees with a ruling on preservation or advance execution, he/she may apply for reconsideration once. The execution of the ruling shall not be suspended during the reconsideration period.

Article 112 For a defendant who must appear in court, if the defendant, after being summoned twice by summons, refuses to appear in court without justifiable reasons, the People's Court may compel his/her appearance.

Article 113 Participants in proceedings and other persons shall observe the courtroom rules.
A People's Court may, for a person who violates the courtroom rules, issue a reprimand, order him/her to leave the courtroom, or impose a fine or detention.
For a person who makes a disturbance or rushes into the courtroom, insults, slanders, threatens, or assaults judicial personnel, or severely disrupts the order of the courtroom, the People's Court shall, in accordance with the law, investigate criminal liability; if the circumstances are relatively minor, a fine or detention shall be imposed.

Article 115 Where parties maliciously collude with each other, attempting through litigation, mediation, or other means to infringe upon the State interests, social public interests, or the legitimate rights and interests of others, the People's Court shall dismiss their request and, depending on the seriousness of the circumstances, impose a fine or detention; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated in accordance with the law.
Where a party unilaterally fabricates the basic facts of a civil case and files a lawsuit with the People's Court, attempting to infringe upon the State interests, social public interests, or the legitimate rights and interests of others, the provisions of the preceding paragraph shall apply.

Article 116 Where a person subject to enforcement maliciously colludes with another person and, through litigation, arbitration, mediation, or other means, evades performing the obligations determined in a legal instrument, the People's Court shall, depending on the seriousness of the circumstances, impose a fine or detention; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated in accordance with the law.

Article 118 The amount of a fine imposed on an individual shall be not more than 100,000 yuan. The amount of a fine imposed on an entity shall be not less than 50,000 yuan and not more than 1,000,000 yuan.
The duration of detention shall be not more than 15 days.
A person detained shall be handed over by the People's Court to the public security organ for custody. During the detention period, if the detained person admits and corrects his/her mistake, the People's Court may decide to lift the detention early.

Article 119 Compulsory appearance, a fine, and detention must be approved by the president of the court.
A compulsory appearance warrant shall be issued for a compulsory appearance.
A written decision shall be used for a fine or detention. If a party disagrees with the decision, he/she may apply to the next higher People's Court for reconsideration once. The enforcement shall not be suspended during the reconsideration period.

Article 120 Compulsory measures against obstruction of civil actions must be decided by the People's Court. If any entity or individual illegally detains another person or illegally distrains another person's property in private to recover a debt, criminal liability shall be investigated in accordance with the law, or detention or a fine shall be imposed.

Article 121: A party engaging in a civil action shall pay the case acceptance fee in accordance with the provisions. For a property case, in addition to the case acceptance fee, other litigation costs shall be paid in accordance with the provisions.
If a party indeed has difficulty paying the litigation costs, the party may, in accordance with the provisions, apply to the People's Court for a deferred payment, a reduced payment, or an exemption.
The measures for collecting litigation costs shall be formulated separately.

Article 123: The prosecution shall file a statement of complaint with the People's Court and provide copies of the complaint according to the number of defendants.
If a party indeed has difficulty in writing a statement of complaint, the party may prosecute orally, and the People's Court shall record it in the record and inform the opposing party.
Article 125: For civil disputes brought by the parties to the People's Court, if mediation is suitable, mediation shall be conducted first, unless the parties refuse mediation.

Article 126: The People's Court shall protect the right of the parties to prosecute in accordance with the provisions of the law. For a prosecution that meets the requirements of Article 122 of this Law, the court must accept the case. If the conditions for prosecution are met, the court shall docket the case within seven days and notify the parties; if the conditions for prosecution are not met, the court shall issue a ruling within seven days and refuse to accept the case. If the plaintiff refuses to accept the ruling, the plaintiff may file an appeal.

Article 128: The People's Court shall, within five days from the date of docketing the case, send a copy of the statement of complaint to the defendant, and the defendant shall, within fifteen days from the date of receipt, submit a statement of defense. The statement of defense shall specify the defendant's name, gender, age, ethnicity, occupation, work unit, domicile, and contact information; the name, domicile, and the name, position, and contact information of the legal representative or principal person in charge of a legal person or any other organization. The People's Court shall, within five days from the date of receiving the statement of defense, send a copy of the statement of defense to the plaintiff.
If the defendant fails to submit a statement of defense, this shall not affect the adjudication by the People's Court.

Article 129: For a case that the People's Court decides to accept, the court shall, in the notice of case acceptance and the notice of responding to the lawsuit, inform the parties of the relevant litigation rights and obligations, or may inform them orally.

Article 130: After the People's Court accepts a case, if a party raises an objection to jurisdiction, the party shall raise it within the period for submitting the statement of defense. The People's Court shall examine the objection raised by the party. If the objection is established, the court shall rule to transfer the case to the People's Court that has jurisdiction; if the objection is not established, the court shall rule to reject it.
If a party does not raise a jurisdictional objection and responds to the lawsuit by submitting a defense or filing a counterclaim, the People's Court hearing the case shall be deemed to have jurisdiction, unless the provisions on hierarchical jurisdiction and exclusive jurisdiction are violated.
Article 131: After the adjudication personnel are determined, the parties shall be informed within three days.
Article 132: The adjudication personnel must carefully examine the litigation materials and investigate and collect necessary evidence.

Article 133: When personnel dispatched by the People's Court conduct an investigation, they shall present their credentials to the person under investigation.
After the investigation record is reviewed by the person under investigation, it shall be signed or sealed by the person under investigation and the investigator.

Article 134: The People's Court may, when necessary, entrust a People's Court in another location to conduct an investigation.
For an entrusted investigation, clear items and requirements must be specified. The entrusted People's Court may proactively supplement the investigation.
After receiving the letter of entrustment, the entrusted People's Court shall complete the investigation within thirty days. If it cannot be completed for any reason, it shall notify the entrusting People's Court by letter within the aforementioned time limit.
Article 135: If a party who must jointly participate in the proceedings fails to do so, the People's Court shall notify that party to participate in the proceedings.

Article 137: The People's Court shall conduct the adjudication of civil cases openly, except where state secrets, personal privacy, or otherwise provided by law are involved.
For divorce cases and cases involving trade secrets, if the parties apply for a closed hearing, a closed hearing may be conducted.
Article 138: The People's Court, when adjudicating civil cases, may conduct circuit trials and handle cases on-site as needed.

Article 139: The People's Court, when adjudicating a civil case, shall notify the parties and other participants in the proceedings three days before the trial. If a trial is open to the public, the court shall announce the names of the parties, the subject matter of the case, and the time and place of the trial.

Article 140: Before the trial hearing, the court clerk shall ascertain whether the parties and other participants in the proceedings are present, and announce the courtroom discipline.
At the commencement of the trial hearing, the presiding judge or the sole judge shall verify the parties, announce the subject matter of the case, announce the list of adjudication personnel, judge's assistants, court clerks, etc., inform the parties of the relevant litigation rights and obligations, and ask the parties whether they have requests for withdrawal.

Article 142: The parties may present new evidence in court.
With the permission of the court, the parties may question witnesses, expert evaluators, and inspectors.
If a party requests a new investigation, expert evaluation, or inspection, the People's Court shall decide whether to grant the request.
Article 143: If the plaintiff increases its claims, the defendant files a counterclaim, or a third party files claims related to the case, these may be tried jointly.

Article 145: After the court debate is concluded, a judgment shall be made according to law. If mediation is possible before the judgment is made, mediation may still be conducted. If mediation fails, a judgment shall be made promptly.

Article 146: If the plaintiff, after being summoned by a subpoena, refuses to appear in court without justifiable reasons, or leaves the courtroom during the trial without permission, the case may be treated as withdrawn; if the defendant has filed a counterclaim, a default judgment may be made.

Article 147: If the defendant, after being summoned by a subpoena, refuses to appear in court without justifiable reasons, or leaves the courtroom during the trial without permission, a default judgment may be made.

Article 148: Before the judgment is pronounced, if the plaintiff applies for withdrawal of the lawsuit, the People's Court shall decide by ruling whether to permit it.
If the People's Court rules not to permit the withdrawal of the lawsuit, and the plaintiff, after being summoned by a subpoena, refuses to appear in court without justifiable reasons, a default judgment may be made.

Article 150: The court clerk shall record all activities of the court hearing in the record, which shall be signed by the adjudication personnel and the court clerk.
The court record shall be read aloud in court, or the parties and other participants in the proceedings may be informed to read it in court or within five days. If the parties or other participants in the proceedings believe that there are omissions or errors in the record of their statements, they have the right to apply for corrections. If corrections are not made, the application shall be recorded in the file.
The court record shall be signed or sealed by the parties and other participants in the proceedings. If a party refuses to sign or seal, the circumstance shall be noted and attached to the file.

Article 151: The People's Court shall publicly pronounce judgments in all cases, whether tried openly or in a closed hearing.
If the judgment is pronounced in court, the written judgment shall be served within ten days; if the judgment is pronounced on a scheduled date, the written judgment shall be issued immediately after pronouncement.
When pronouncing a judgment, the court must inform the parties of their right to appeal, the appeal period, and the court to which the appeal shall be filed.
When pronouncing a divorce judgment, the court must inform the parties that they shall not remarry before the judgment takes legal effect.

Article 152: For a case tried by the People's Court under the ordinary procedure, the trial shall be concluded within six months from the date of docketing. If there are special circumstances requiring an extension, with the approval of the president of the court, the extension may be for up to six months; if further extension is needed, the approval of the higher People's Court shall be obtained.
Article 156: If, during the trial of a case by the People's Court, some of the facts are already clear, a judgment may be made on that part first.

Article 158: Judgments and rulings of the Supreme People's Court, and judgments and rulings that are not subject to appeal according to law or that have not been appealed within the time limit for appeal, are legally effective judgments and rulings.
Article 159: The public may access legally effective written judgments and written rulings, except for content involving state secrets, trade secrets, or personal privacy.

Article 160: For simple civil cases where the facts are clear, the rights and obligations are definite, and the dispute is minor, tried by a Primary People's Court and its dispatched tribunals, the provisions of this Chapter shall apply.
For civil cases other than those specified in the preceding paragraph, tried by a Primary People's Court and its dispatched tribunals, the parties may also agree to apply the summary procedure.

Article 161 In a simple civil action, the plaintiff may file an oral complaint.
The parties may simultaneously appear before the Primary People's Court or its dispatched tribunal to request settlement of the dispute. The Primary People's Court or its dispatched tribunal may hear the case immediately or set a later date for hearing.

Article 162 When the Primary People's Court and its dispatched tribunal hear a simple civil action, they may summon the parties and witnesses, serve litigation documents, and hear the case in a simplified manner, provided that the parties' right to state their opinions shall be protected.
Article 163 A simple civil action shall be tried by a single judge alone, and shall not be subject to the restrictions provided in Articles 139, 141, and 144 of this Law.

Article 164 When a People's Court tries a case under the summary procedure, it shall conclude the case within three months from the date of case filing. If an extension is necessary due to special circumstances, it may be extended by one month upon approval by the president of the court.

Article 165 When the Primary People's Court and its dispatched tribunal hear a simple civil case involving monetary payment with clear facts, definite rights and obligations, and minor disputes, where the subject matter amount does not exceed 50% of the average annual salary of employed persons in the relevant province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government in the previous year, the small-claim procedure shall be applied, and the judgment shall be final.
When the Primary People's Court and its dispatched tribunal hear a civil case as provided in the preceding paragraph, where the subject matter amount exceeds 50% but is less than twice the average annual salary of employed persons in the relevant province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government in the previous year, the parties may agree to apply the small-claim procedure.
Article 167 When a People's Court tries a case under the small-claim procedure, it may conclude the case in a single hearing and pronounce the judgment in court.

Article 168 When a People's Court tries a case under the small-claim procedure, it shall conclude the case within two months from the date of case filing. If an extension is necessary due to special circumstances, it may be extended by one month upon approval by the president of the court.

Article 169 If, during the trial, a People's Court finds that a case is unsuitable for the small-claim procedure, it shall apply other provisions of the summary procedure or rule to convert to the ordinary procedure.
If a party considers that the trial of a case under the small-claim procedure violates legal provisions, it may raise an objection with the People's Court. The People's Court shall examine the objection raised by the party; if the objection is established, it shall apply other provisions of the summary procedure or rule to convert to the ordinary procedure; if the objection is not established, it shall rule to dismiss it.
Article 170 If, during the trial, a People's Court finds that a case is unsuitable for the summary procedure, it shall rule to convert to the ordinary procedure.

Article 171 A party who refuses to accept a first-instance judgment of a local People's Court shall have the right to file an appeal with the next higher People's Court within fifteen days from the date of service of the written judgment.
A party who refuses to accept a first-instance ruling of a local People's Court shall have the right to file an appeal with the next higher People's Court within ten days from the date of service of the written ruling.

Article 172 An appeal shall be filed by submitting a written appeal petition. The contents of the written appeal petition shall include the names of the parties, the name of the legal person and the name of its legal representative, or the name of any other organization and the name of its principal responsible person; the name of the original People's Court, the case number, and the cause of action; and the requests and grounds for the appeal.

Article 173 The written appeal petition shall be submitted through the original People's Court, and copies thereof shall be provided in accordance with the number of the opposing parties or representatives.
If a party files an appeal directly with the second-instance People's Court, the second-instance People's Court shall, within five days, transmit the written appeal petition to the original People's Court.

Article 174 Upon receipt of the written appeal petition, the original People's Court shall, within five days, serve a copy thereof on the opposing party, who shall file a written defense within fifteen days from the date of receipt. The People's Court shall, within five days from the date of receipt of the written defense, serve a copy thereof on the appellant. The failure of the opposing party to file a written defense shall not affect the trial by the People's Court.
Upon receipt of the written appeal petition and the written defense, the original People's Court shall, within five days, transmit them together with the entire case file and evidence to the second-instance People's Court.
Article 175 The second-instance People's Court shall examine the facts and the application of the law relating to the appeal requests.

Article 176 The second-instance People's Court shall hear an appealed case in open court. After reviewing the case file, conducting investigations, and questioning the parties, if no new facts, evidence, or grounds are presented and the People's Court considers that an open court trial is unnecessary, it may hold a hearing without an open court trial.
The second-instance People's Court may hear an appealed case at its own seat or at the place where the case arose or the seat of the original People's Court.
Article 178 A ruling shall uniformly be used in handling appealed cases against rulings of the first-instance People's Court by the second-instance People's Court.

Article 179 The second-instance People's Court may conduct mediation in hearing an appealed case. If a mediation agreement is reached, a mediation document shall be prepared, signed by the trial judges and the clerk, and sealed with the seal of the People's Court. Upon service of the mediation document, the judgment of the original People's Court shall be deemed revoked.

Article 180 Before a judgment is pronounced by the second-instance People's Court, if the appellant applies to withdraw the appeal, whether to permit such withdrawal shall be determined by the second-instance People's Court by ruling.
Article 181 The second-instance People's Court shall, in hearing an appealed case, apply the first-instance ordinary procedure, except as otherwise provided in this Chapter.
Article 182 The judgments and rulings of the second-instance People's Court are final.

Article 183 When a People's Court hears an appealed case against a judgment, it shall conclude the case within three months from the date of case filing for the second instance. If an extension is necessary due to special circumstances, it shall be approved by the president of the court.
When a People's Court hears an appealed case against a ruling, it shall render a final ruling within thirty days from the date of case filing for the second instance.

Article 184 The provisions of this Chapter shall apply when a People's Court hears cases concerning the qualifications of voters, declaration of disappearance or death, designation of estate administrators, determination of a citizen as having no or limited civil capacity, determination of ownerless property, confirmation of mediation agreements, and realization of security interests. Matters not provided for in this Chapter shall be governed by the relevant provisions of this Law and other laws.

Article 185 Cases adjudicated under the procedure of this Chapter shall be finally adjudicated at first instance. Cases concerning voter qualifications or major and difficult cases shall be tried by a collegial panel composed of judges; other cases shall be tried by a single judge alone.

Article 186 If, in the course of trying a case under the procedure of this Chapter, a People's Court finds that the case involves a dispute over civil rights and interests, it shall rule to terminate the special procedure and inform interested parties that they may file a separate prosecution.

Article 187 When a People's Court tries a case under the special procedure, it shall conclude the case within thirty days from the date of case filing or within thirty days after the expiration of the period of public notice. If an extension is necessary due to special circumstances, it shall be approved by the president of the court, except for cases concerning voter qualifications.

Article 188 A citizen who refuses to accept the decision made by the election committee regarding a complaint about voter qualifications may file a lawsuit with the Primary People's Court in the place where the electoral district is located within five days before the election day.

Article 189 After accepting a case concerning voter qualifications, the People's Court must conclude the case before the election day.
During the hearing, the plaintiff, the representative of the election committee, and the relevant citizens must appear.
The written judgment of the People's Court shall be served on the election committee and the plaintiff before the election day, and the relevant citizens shall be notified.

Article 190 If a citizen has been missing for two full years, an interested party applying for declaration of his or her disappearance shall submit the application to the Primary People's Court in the place of domicile of the missing person.
The application shall state the facts, time, and request of disappearance, and shall attach a written certification from the public security organ or other relevant organ regarding the missing citizen's whereabouts.

Article 191 If a citizen has been missing for four full years, or has been missing due to an accident for two full years, or has been missing due to an accident and the relevant organ certifies that the citizen is unlikely to survive, an interested party applying for declaration of his or her death shall submit the application to the Primary People's Court in the place of domicile of the missing person.
The application shall state the facts, time, and request of disappearance, and shall attach a written certification from the public security organ or other relevant organ regarding the missing citizen's whereabouts.

Article 192 After accepting a case for declaration of disappearance or death, the People's Court shall issue a public notice seeking the missing person. The period of public notice for declaration of disappearance shall be three months, and the period of public notice for declaration of death shall be one year. If the person is missing due to an accident and the relevant organ certifies that the citizen is unlikely to survive, the period of public notice for declaration of death shall be three months.
Upon expiration of the period of public notice, the People's Court shall render a judgment declaring disappearance or death or dismiss the application, based on whether the facts of disappearance or death are confirmed.
Article 193 If a citizen declared disappeared or dead reappears, upon application by the citizen or an interested party, the People's Court shall render a new judgment revoking the original judgment.

Article 194 If there is a dispute over the appointment of an estate administrator, an interested party applying for designation of an estate administrator shall submit the application to the Primary People's Court in the place of domicile of the deceased at the time of death or the place where the principal estate is located.
The application shall state the time of death of the deceased, the grounds for application, and specific requests, and shall attach relevant evidence of the deceased's death.

Article 195 After accepting an application, the People's Court shall examine and verify the matter, and shall render a judgment designating the estate administrator in accordance with the principle of facilitating estate administration.

Article 196 If a designated estate administrator dies, terminates, loses civil capacity, or is otherwise unable to continue performing estate administration duties, the People's Court may designate another estate administrator upon application by an interested party or the administrator himself or herself.

Article 197 If an estate administrator violates estate administration duties and seriously infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of heirs, legatees, or creditors, the People's Court may, upon application by an interested party, revoke the qualification of the estate administrator and designate a new estate administrator according to law.

Article 198 An application for determining a citizen as having no or limited civil capacity shall be submitted to the Primary People's Court in the place of domicile of the citizen by an interested party or a relevant organization.
The application shall state the facts and grounds for the citizen's lack or limitation of civil capacity.

Article 199 After accepting an application, the People's Court shall, when necessary, have the citizen sought to be determined as having no or limited civil capacity undergo an expert evaluation. If the applicant has already provided an opinion of expert evaluation, the People's Court shall examine such opinion.

Article 200 When a People's Court tries a case for determining a citizen as having no or limited civil capacity, a close relative of the citizen shall serve as the agent ad litem, except for the applicant. If the close relatives shift responsibility among themselves, the People's Court shall designate one of them as the agent ad litem. If the citizen's health permits, the citizen's own opinion shall also be sought.
If, after trial, the People's Court finds that the application is supported by factual grounds, it shall render a judgment determining the citizen as having no or limited civil capacity; if it finds that the application is not supported by factual grounds, it shall render a judgment dismissing the application.

Article 201 Where a People's Court, upon the application of a person who has been determined to be a person without or with limited capacity for civil conduct, an interested party, or a relevant organization, verifies that the causes for such person to be without or with limited capacity for civil conduct have been eliminated, it shall render a new judgment and revoke the original judgment.

Article 202 An application for determining property as ownerless shall be filed by a citizen, legal person or any other organization with the Primary People's Court of the place where the property is located. The application shall state the type and quantity of the property and the grounds for requesting the determination of the property as ownerless.

Article 203 After accepting an application and upon examination and verification, the People's Court shall issue a public notice for claiming the property. If no claim is made within one year from the issuance of the public notice, the court shall, by judgment, determine the property as ownerless and vest it in the State or a collective.

Article 204 After a judgment has determined property as ownerless, if the original owner or heir of the property appears and makes a claim within the limitation of action prescribed by the Civil Code, the People's Court shall, after verifying the claim, render a new judgment and revoke the original judgment.

Article 206 After accepting an application and upon examination, if the application complies with the provisions of law, the People's Court shall rule that the mediation agreement is effective; if one party refuses to perform or fails to fully perform the agreement, the other party may apply to the People's Court for enforcement. If the application does not comply with the provisions of law, the court shall rule to dismiss the application; the parties may modify the original mediation agreement or reach a new mediation agreement through mediation, or may initiate an action in the People's Court.

Article 207 An application for realizing a security interest shall be filed by the security interest holder and any other person entitled to request the realization of the security interest with the Primary People's Court of the place where the secured property is located or where the security interest is registered, in accordance with laws such as the Civil Code.

Article 208 After accepting an application and upon examination, if the application complies with the provisions of law, the People's Court shall rule to auction or sell off the secured property, and the parties may apply to the People's Court for enforcement based on the ruling; if the application does not comply with the provisions of law, the court shall rule to dismiss the application, and the parties may initiate an action in the People's Court.

Article 209 Where the president of a People's Court at any level finds that a legally effective judgment, ruling, or mediation document of that court indeed contains an error and deems it necessary to conduct a retrial, the matter shall be submitted to the judicial committee for discussion and decision.
Where the Supreme People's Court finds that a legally effective judgment, ruling, or mediation document of a local People's Court at any level indeed contains an error, or where a People's Court at a higher level finds that a legally effective judgment, ruling, or mediation document of a People's Court at a lower level indeed contains an error, it has the authority to bring the case up for trial or to direct the lower People's Court to conduct a retrial.

Article 210 Where a party to a legally effective judgment or ruling considers that it contains an error, the party may apply for a retrial with the People's Court at the next higher level; however, in cases where one party involves a large number of persons or both parties are citizens, the application may also be filed with the original trial People's Court. The filing of an application for retrial by a party shall not suspend the enforcement of the judgment or ruling.

Article 212 Where a party to a legally effective mediation document submits evidence proving that the mediation violated the principle of voluntariness or that the content of the mediation agreement violates the law, the party may apply for a retrial. If the People's Court, upon examination, verifies the facts, it shall conduct a retrial.
Article 213 A party shall not apply for retrial of a legally effective judgment or mediation document dissolving a marital relationship.

Article 214 Where a party applies for a retrial, the party shall submit a written application for retrial and other materials. The People's Court shall, within five days from receipt of the application for retrial, send a copy of the application to the other party. The other party shall submit a written opinion within fifteen days from receipt of the copy of the application; failure to submit a written opinion shall not affect the examination by the People's Court. The People's Court may require the applicant and the other party to supplement relevant materials and inquire about relevant matters.

Article 215 The People's Court shall examine the application for retrial within three months from receipt of the application; if it complies with the provisions of this Law, it shall rule to conduct a retrial; if it does not comply, it shall rule to dismiss the application. In exceptional circumstances requiring an extension, such extension shall be approved by the president of the court.
Cases in which a retrial is ordered upon the application of a party shall be tried by a People's Court at or above the level of an Intermediate People's Court, except where the party, in accordance with Article 210 of this Law, elects to apply for retrial to a Primary People's Court. Cases in which a retrial is ordered by the Supreme People's Court or a Higher People's Court shall be retried by that court or referred to another People's Court for retrial, and may also be referred to the original trial People's Court for retrial.

Article 216 A party applying for a retrial shall file the application within six months after the judgment or ruling takes legal effect; in circumstances falling under items (1), (3), (12), or (13) of Article 211 of this Law, the application shall be filed within six months from the date the party knows or should have known of such circumstances.

Article 217 For a case in which a retrial is decided in accordance with the trial supervision procedure, the court shall rule to suspend the enforcement of the original judgment, ruling, or mediation document; however, for cases involving claims for alimony, maintenance, child support, pensions for the disabled or survivors of the deceased, medical expenses, or labor remuneration, the enforcement may not be suspended.

Article 218 Where a People's Court retries a case in accordance with the trial supervision procedure, if the legally effective judgment or ruling was rendered by a court of first instance, the case shall be tried in accordance with the procedure of first instance, and the parties may appeal the judgment or ruling rendered; if the legally effective judgment or ruling was rendered by a court of second instance, the case shall be tried in accordance with the procedure of second instance, and the judgment or ruling rendered shall be legally effective; if a People's Court at a higher level brings the case up for trial in accordance with the trial supervision procedure, the case shall be tried in accordance with the procedure of second instance, and the judgment or ruling rendered shall be legally effective.
When a People's Court retries a case, it shall form a new collegial panel.

Article 219 Where the Supreme People's Procuratorate finds that a legally effective judgment or ruling of a People's Court at any level, or a People's Procuratorate at a higher level finds that a legally effective judgment or ruling of a People's Court at a lower level, falls under any of the circumstances specified in Article 211 of this Law, or discovers that a mediation document impairs the national interest or the public interest, it shall file a protest.
Where a local People's Procuratorate at any level finds that a legally effective judgment or ruling of a People's Court at the corresponding level falls under any of the circumstances specified in Article 211 of this Law, or discovers that a mediation document impairs the national interest or the public interest, it may issue a procuratorial recommendation to the People's Court at the corresponding level and report it to the People's Procuratorate at a higher level for record; it may also request the People's Procuratorate at a higher level to file a protest with the People's Court at the corresponding level.
People's Procuratorates at all levels have the authority to issue a procuratorial recommendation to the People's Court at the corresponding level regarding the illegal conduct of judicial officers in trial procedures other than the trial supervision procedure.

Article 221 Where necessary for fulfilling the duty of legal supervision in issuing a procuratorial recommendation or filing a protest, the People's Procuratorate may investigate and verify relevant circumstances with the parties or persons outside the case.

Article 222 For a case in which the People's Procuratorate files a protest, the People's Court that accepts the protest shall, within thirty days from receipt of the protest letter, rule to conduct a retrial; if the case falls under any of the circumstances specified in items (1) through (5) of Article 211 of this Law, the court may refer the case to the next lower People's Court for retrial, except where such lower court has already conducted a retrial.
Article 223 Where the People's Procuratorate decides to file a protest against a judgment, ruling, or mediation document of a People's Court, it shall prepare a protest letter.

Article 224 For a case in which the People's Procuratorate files a protest, when the People's Court conducts the retrial, it shall notify the People's Procuratorate to send a representative to appear in court.

Article 225 Where a creditor requests the debtor to pay a sum of money or negotiable instruments, and the following conditions are met, the creditor may apply for an order for payment to the Primary People's Court that has jurisdiction:
(1) There is no other debt dispute between the creditor and the debtor;
