(2) The order for payment can be served on the debtor.
The application shall clearly state the amount of money or negotiable instruments requested and the facts and evidence on which the request is based.
Article 226 After a creditor files an application, the People's Court shall, within five days, notify the creditor whether the application is accepted.

Article 227 After accepting an application and examining the facts and evidence provided by the creditor, if the debt relationship is clear and lawful, the People's Court shall, within fifteen days from the date of acceptance, issue an order for payment to the debtor; if the application is unfounded, the court shall rule to dismiss it.
The debtor shall, within fifteen days from receipt of the order for payment, pay off the debt or submit a written objection to the People's Court.
If the debtor neither raises an objection nor complies with the order for payment within the time limit specified in the preceding paragraph, the creditor may apply to the People's Court for enforcement.

Article 228 After receiving a written objection submitted by the debtor, the People's Court shall, upon examination, if the objection is valid, rule to terminate the supervision procedure, and the order for payment shall automatically lose effect.
If the order for payment loses effect, the case shall be transferred to an action procedure, except where the party that applied for the order for payment does not consent to initiating an action.

Article 229 Where an instrument that may be transferred by endorsement according to relevant provisions is stolen, lost, or destroyed, the holder of the instrument may apply for a public notice of exhortation to the Primary People's Court of the place of payment of the instrument. The provisions of this Chapter shall apply to other matters for which a public notice of exhortation may be applied for according to law.
The applicant shall submit an application to the People's Court, stating the face amount, the drawer, the holder, the endorsers and other main contents of the instrument, as well as the reasons and facts for the application.

Article 230 Where the People's Court decides to accept an application, it shall simultaneously notify the payer to suspend payment, and shall, within three days, issue a public notice urging interested parties to claim their rights. The period of the public notice of exhortation shall be determined by the People's Court based on the circumstances, but shall not be less than sixty days.

Article 231 Upon receipt of the notice from the People's Court to suspend payment, the payer shall suspend payment until the conclusion of the public notice of exhortation procedure.
Any act of transferring rights under the instrument during the period of the public notice of exhortation shall be void.

Article 232 An interested party shall make a claim to the People's Court during the period of the public notice of exhortation.
After receiving the claim from an interested party, the People's Court shall rule to terminate the public notice of exhortation procedure and notify the applicant and the payer.
The applicant or the claimant may initiate an action in the People's Court.

Article 233 If no claim is made, the People's Court shall, upon the application of the applicant, render a judgment declaring the instrument void. The judgment shall be publicly announced and the payer shall be notified. From the date of the public announcement of the judgment, the applicant has the right to request payment from the payer.

Article 234 If an interested party, for good reason, was unable to make a claim to the People's Court before the judgment, the party may, within one year from the date the party knows or should have known of the public announcement of the judgment, initiate an action in the People's Court that rendered the judgment.

Article 235 Legally effective civil judgments and rulings, as well as the property-related parts of criminal judgments and rulings, shall be enforced by the People's Court of first instance or by the People's Court at the same level as the court of first instance of the place where the property subject to enforcement is located.
Other legal documents that shall be enforced by a People's Court according to law shall be enforced by the People's Court of the place of the domicile of the person subject to enforcement or the place where the property subject to enforcement is located.

Article 236 Where a party or an interested party considers that an enforcement act violates legal provisions, the party may submit a written objection to the People's Court responsible for enforcement. Where a party or an interested party submits a written objection, the People's Court shall examine it within fifteen days from receipt of the written objection; if the reasons are valid, the court shall rule to rescind or correct the act; if the reasons are not valid, the court shall rule to dismiss the objection. If a party or an interested party is dissatisfied with the ruling, the party may, within ten days from the date the ruling is served, apply to the People's Court at the next higher level for reconsideration.

Article 237 Where a People's Court fails to enforce within six months from receipt of the application for enforcement, the applicant for enforcement may apply to the People's Court at the next higher level for enforcement. Upon examination, the People's Court at the next higher level may order the original People's Court to enforce within a specified period, or may decide to enforce the matter itself or direct another People's Court to enforce it.

Article 238 During the enforcement process, if a person outside the case submits a written objection to the subject matter of enforcement, the People's Court shall examine it within fifteen days from receipt of the written objection; if the reasons are valid, the court shall rule to suspend enforcement against that subject matter; if the reasons are not valid, the court shall rule to dismiss the objection. If the person outside the case or the party is dissatisfied with the ruling and believes that the original judgment or ruling contains an error, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the trial supervision procedure; if the matter is unrelated to the original judgment or ruling, the party may, within fifteen days from the date the ruling is served, initiate an action in the People's Court.

Article 239 Enforcement work shall be carried out by an enforcement officer.
When taking compulsory enforcement measures, the enforcement officer shall present identification. After enforcement is completed, a record of the enforcement shall be made, signed or sealed by the relevant persons present.
A People's Court may establish an enforcement organ as needed.

Article 240 Where the person subject to enforcement or the property subject to enforcement is located in another locality, the original court may entrust the local People's Court with the enforcement. The entrusted People's Court shall, within fifteen days from receipt of the letter of entrustment, commence enforcement and shall not refuse to do so. After completing enforcement, the entrusted court shall promptly inform the entrusting court of the enforcement result in writing; if enforcement is not completed within thirty days, the entrusted court shall also inform the entrusting court of the enforcement status in writing.
If the entrusted People's Court fails to enforce within fifteen days from receipt of the letter of entrustment, the entrusting People's Court may request the People's Court at a higher level over the entrusted court to direct the entrusted court to enforce.

Article 241 During enforcement, if the parties reach a settlement agreement on their own, the enforcement officer shall record the contents of the agreement in the笔录, and the parties shall sign or affix their seals thereto.
If the applicant for execution reaches a settlement agreement with the person subject to execution due to fraud or duress, or if any party fails to perform the settlement agreement, the People's Court may, upon application by the party, resume enforcement of the original effective legal document.

Article 242 During enforcement, if the person subject to execution provides a guaranty to the People's Court with the consent of the applicant for execution, the People's Court may decide to suspend the enforcement and the period of such suspension. If the person subject to execution fails to perform within the extended period, the People's Court shall have the authority to enforce against the guaranty property of the person subject to execution or the property of the guarantor.

Article 243 If a citizen who is the person subject to execution dies, the estate shall be used to satisfy the debts. If a legal person or other organization that is the person subject to execution is terminated, the successor of its rights and obligations shall perform the obligations.

Article 244 After enforcement is completed, if the judgment, ruling, or other legal document on the basis of which enforcement was carried out is indeed erroneous and is revoked by the People's Court, the People's Court shall issue a ruling ordering the person who obtained the property to return it; if the person refuses to return it, compulsory execution shall be carried out.
Article 245 The enforcement of a mediation agreement made by the People's Court shall be governed by the provisions of this Part.
Article 246 The People's Procuratorate shall have the authority to exercise legal supervision over civil enforcement activities.

Article 247 A party shall perform a legally effective civil judgment or ruling. If one party refuses to perform, the other party may apply to the People's Court for enforcement, or the adjudicator may refer the matter to the enforcement officer for enforcement.
A party shall perform a mediation agreement or other legal document that shall be enforced by the People's Court. If one party refuses to perform, the other party may apply to the People's Court for enforcement.

Article 249 For a notarized debt document that is given compulsory enforcement effect according to law by the notarial authority, if one party fails to perform, the other party may apply to the competent People's Court for enforcement, and the People's Court to which application is made shall enforce.
If the notarized debt document is indeed erroneous, the People's Court shall rule not to enforce it, and shall serve the ruling on the parties and the notarial authority.

Article 250 The period for applying for enforcement shall be two years. The suspension or interruption of the limitation period for applying for enforcement shall be governed by the provisions of law regarding the suspension or interruption of limitation of action.
The period provided in the preceding paragraph shall be calculated from the last day of the period for performance specified in the legal document; if the legal document provides for performance in installments, it shall be calculated from the date on which the period for performance of the last installment expires; if the legal document does not specify a period for performance, it shall be calculated from the date on which the legal document takes effect.

Article 251 Upon receipt of a written application for enforcement or a written referral for enforcement, the enforcement officer shall issue an enforcement notice to the person subject to execution, and may immediately take compulsory enforcement measures.

Article 252 If the person subject to execution fails to perform the obligations specified in the legal document in accordance with the enforcement notice, the person shall report the current state of property and the state of property for the year prior to the date of receipt of the enforcement notice. If the person subject to execution refuses to report or makes a false report, the People's Court may, depending on the gravity of the circumstances, impose a fine or detention on the person subject to execution, or on the legal representative of the person or the principal leading person or directly responsible person of the relevant unit.

Article 253 If the person subject to execution fails to perform the obligations specified in the legal document in accordance with the enforcement notice, the People's Court shall have the authority to inquire with relevant units about the property of the person subject to execution, such as deposits, bonds, stocks, fund shares, etc. The People's Court shall have the authority to seize, freeze, transfer, or sell off the property of the person subject to execution under different circumstances. The property inquired about, seized, frozen, transferred, or sold off by the People's Court shall not exceed the scope of the obligations that the person subject to execution shall perform.
When the People's Court decides to seize, freeze, transfer, or sell off property, it shall issue a ruling and issue a notice of assistance in enforcement, and the relevant unit must comply.

Article 254 If the person subject to execution fails to perform the obligations specified in the legal document in accordance with the enforcement notice, the People's Court shall have the authority to withhold or withdraw the portion of the income of the person subject to execution that shall be used to perform the obligations. However, the necessary living expenses for the person subject to execution and the dependents supported by the person shall be reserved.
When the People's Court withholds or withdraws income, it shall issue a ruling and issue a notice of assistance in enforcement, and the unit where the person subject to execution works, the bank, the credit cooperative, and other units with savings business must comply.

Article 255 If the person subject to execution fails to perform the obligations specified in the legal document in accordance with the enforcement notice, the People's Court shall have the authority to seal up, seize, freeze, auction, or sell off the portion of the property of the person subject to execution that shall be used to perform the obligations. However, the daily necessities for the person subject to execution and the dependents supported by the person shall be reserved.
When taking the measures provided in the preceding paragraph, the People's Court shall issue a ruling.

Article 256 When the People's Court seals up or seizes property, if the person subject to execution is a citizen, the person subject to execution or his adult family members shall be notified to be present; if the person subject to execution is a legal person or other organization, its legal representative or principal leading person shall be notified to be present. Refusal to be present shall not affect the enforcement. If the person subject to execution is a citizen, the work unit of the person or the grass-roots organization in the place where the property is located shall send personnel to participate.
For the property sealed up or seized, the enforcement officer must prepare an inventory, which shall be signed or affixed with seals by the persons present, and then a copy shall be given to the person subject to execution. If the person subject to execution is a citizen, a copy may also be given to his adult family members.

Article 257 For property sealed up, the enforcement officer may designate the person subject to execution to be responsible for custody. Losses caused by the fault of the person subject to execution shall be borne by the person subject to execution.

Article 258 After property is sealed up or seized, the enforcement officer shall order the person subject to execution to perform the obligations specified in the legal document within a specified period. If the person subject to execution fails to perform within the extended period, the People's Court shall auction the sealed-up or seized property; if the property is not suitable for auction or if the parties agree not to conduct an auction, the People's Court may entrust a relevant unit to sell off the property or sell it off itself. Articles prohibited by the State from free trading shall be delivered to the relevant unit for purchase at the price prescribed by the State.

Article 259 If the person subject to execution fails to perform the obligations specified in the legal document and conceals property, the People's Court shall have the authority to issue a search warrant to search the person subject to execution and the premises of the person or the place where property is concealed.
When taking the measures provided in the preceding paragraph, the search warrant shall be signed by the president of the court.

Article 260 For money or goods or negotiable instruments designated for delivery in a legal document, the enforcement officer shall summon the parties to deliver them face to face, or the enforcement officer shall transfer them, and the person to whom they are delivered shall sign a receipt.
If a relevant unit holds such money or goods or negotiable instruments, it shall transfer them in accordance with the notice of assistance in enforcement of the People's Court, and the person to whom they are delivered shall sign a receipt.
If a relevant citizen holds such money or goods or negotiable instruments, the People's Court shall notify the citizen to surrender them. If the citizen refuses to surrender them, compulsory execution shall be carried out.

Article 261 For compulsory removal from a house or compulsory vacation of land, the president of the court shall issue a public notice, ordering the person subject to execution to perform within a specified period. If the person subject to execution fails to perform within the extended period, the enforcement officer shall carry out compulsory execution.
During compulsory execution, if the person subject to execution is a citizen, the person subject to execution or his adult family members shall be notified to be present; if the person subject to execution is a legal person or other organization, its legal representative or principal leading person shall be notified to be present. Refusal to be present shall not affect the enforcement. If the person subject to execution is a citizen, the work unit of the person or the grass-roots organization in the place where the house or land is located shall send personnel to participate. The enforcement officer shall record the circumstances of the compulsory execution in the笔录, which shall be signed or affixed with seals by the persons present.
The property removed during compulsory removal from the house shall be transported by personnel of the People's Court to a designated location and delivered to the person subject to execution. If the person subject to execution is a citizen, it may also be delivered to his adult family members. Losses caused by refusal to accept delivery shall be borne by the person subject to execution.

Article 262 During enforcement, if it is necessary to go through the formalities for the transfer of certificates of property rights, the People's Court may issue a notice of assistance in enforcement to the relevant unit, and the relevant unit must comply.

Article 263 For acts designated in judgments, rulings, or other legal documents, if the person subject to execution fails to perform in accordance with the enforcement notice, the People's Court may carry out compulsory execution or entrust the act to a relevant unit or other person to complete, and the expenses shall be borne by the person subject to execution.

Article 264 If the person subject to execution fails to perform the obligation to pay money within the period specified in a judgment, ruling, or other legal document, the person shall pay double the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance. If the person subject to execution fails to perform other obligations within the period specified in a judgment, ruling, or other legal document, the person shall pay a surcharge for delayed performance.

Article 265 After the People's Court has taken the enforcement measures provided for in Article 253, Article 254, and Article 255 of this Law, if the person subject to execution is still unable to repay the debt, the person shall continue to perform the obligation. If the creditor discovers that the person subject to execution has other property, the creditor may at any time request the People's Court to enforce.

Article 266 If the person subject to execution fails to perform the obligations specified in the legal document, the People's Court may impose or notify the relevant unit to assist in imposing measures such as restricting the person from leaving the country, recording the information in the credit reference system, publishing the information of non-performance through media, and other measures provided by law.
Article 269 The ruling to suspend or terminate enforcement shall take immediate effect upon service on the parties.

Article 270 Civil actions involving foreign element conducted within the territory of the People's Republic of China shall be governed by the provisions of this Part. Where this Part does not provide otherwise, the other relevant provisions of this Law shall apply.

Article 271 Where an international treaty concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China contains provisions that differ from those of this Law, the provisions of that international treaty shall apply, except for the provisions on which the People's Republic of China has declared reservations.

Article 272 Civil actions instituted against a foreign national, foreign organization, or international organization enjoying diplomatic privileges and immunities shall be handled in accordance with the relevant laws of the People's Republic of China and the provisions of international treaties concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China.

Article 273 When adjudicating a civil case involving foreign element, the People's Court shall use the spoken and written languages commonly used in the People's Republic of China. If a party requests the provision of interpretation, it may be provided, and the expenses shall be borne by the party.

Article 274 If a foreign national, stateless person, foreign enterprise, or organization instructs a lawyer to represent the party in prosecution or defense before the People's Court, the party must instruct a lawyer of the People's Republic of China.

Article 275 If a foreign national, stateless person, foreign enterprise, or organization with no domicile within the territory of the People's Republic of China instructs a lawyer of the People's Republic of China or any other person to represent the party in litigation, the power of attorney sent or entrusted from outside the territory of the People's Republic of China shall become effective only after it is notarized by a notarial authority in the country of domicile and authenticated by the embassy or consulate of the People's Republic of China in that country, or after the certification formalities prescribed in the relevant treaty concluded between the People's Republic of China and that country are fulfilled.

Article 276 For a civil dispute involving foreign element, if an action is instituted against a defendant with no domicile within the territory of the People's Republic of China, other than an action concerning personal status, and if the place of contracting of the contract, the place of performance of the contract, the location of the subject matter of the action, the location of the property available for seizure, the location of the tortious act, or the location of the representative office is within the territory of the People's Republic of China, the action may be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court of the place of contracting, place of performance, location of the subject matter, location of property available for seizure, location of the tortious act, or location of the representative office.
In addition to the provisions of the preceding paragraph, if a civil dispute involving foreign element has any other appropriate connection with the People's Republic of China, it may be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court.

Article 277 If the parties to a civil dispute involving foreign element agree in writing to choose the People's Court for jurisdiction, the dispute may be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court.
Article 278 If a party does not raise an objection to jurisdiction and responds to the action or files a counterclaim, the People's Court shall be deemed to have jurisdiction.

Article 280 For the same dispute between the parties, if one party institutes an action in a foreign court and the other party institutes an action in the People's Court, or if one party institutes an action both in a foreign court and in the People's Court, the People's Court may accept the case if it has jurisdiction according to this Law. If the parties have entered into an exclusive jurisdiction agreement choosing the jurisdiction of a foreign court and this does not violate the provisions of this Law on exclusive jurisdiction and does not involve the sovereignty, security, or public interest of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court may rule not to accept the case; if it has already accepted the case, it shall rule to dismiss the action.

If, after the People's Court accepts a case pursuant to the preceding article, a party applies in writing for the People's Court to suspend the action on the ground that a foreign court has already accepted the case prior to the People's Court, the People's Court may order suspension of the action, unless any of the following circumstances exists:
(1) the parties have agreed by agreement to choose the jurisdiction of the People's Court, or the dispute falls within the exclusive jurisdiction of the People's Court;
(2) it is manifestly more convenient for the People's Court to adjudicate the case.
If the foreign court fails to take necessary measures to adjudicate the case or fails to conclude the case within a reasonable period, upon the party's written application, the People's Court shall resume the action.
If a legally effective judgment or ruling made by a foreign court has been wholly or partially recognized by the People's Court, and the party institutes a new action before the People's Court with respect to the part that has been recognized, the People's Court shall rule that the prosecution is not to be accepted; if it has already been accepted, the People's Court shall rule that the prosecution is to be dismissed.

If the defendant has no domicile within the territory of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall serve a copy of the statement of complaint on the defendant and notify the defendant to submit a statement of defense within thirty days after receipt of the copy of the statement of complaint. Whether an extension applied for by the defendant shall be granted shall be decided by the People's Court.

A party who has no domicile within the territory of the People's Republic of China and who is dissatisfied with a judgment or ruling of a first-instance People's Court shall have the right to file an appeal within thirty days from the date of service of the judgment or ruling. The respondent shall, after receiving a copy of the statement of appeal, submit a statement of defense within thirty days. Whether an extension applied for by a party who is unable to file an appeal or submit a statement of defense within the statutory period shall be granted shall be decided by the People's Court.
The time periods for the People's Court to adjudicate foreign-related civil actions shall not be subject to the restrictions provided for in Articles 152 and 183 of this Law.

For disputes arising from foreign-related economic and trade, transport, and maritime activities, if the parties have included an arbitration clause in the contract or subsequently concluded a written arbitration agreement to submit the dispute for arbitration to a foreign-related arbitration institution of the People's Republic of China or another arbitration institution, the parties shall not institute an action before the People's Court.
If the parties have not included an arbitration clause in the contract or have not subsequently concluded a written arbitration agreement, they may institute an action before the People's Court.

If a party applies for preservation measures, the foreign-related arbitration institution of the People's Republic of China shall submit the party's application to the Intermediate People's Court of the place where the respondent has its domicile or where the property is located for a ruling.

If a dispute has been arbitrated by a foreign-related arbitration institution of the People's Republic of China, the parties shall not institute an action before the People's Court. If one party fails to perform the arbitration award, the other party may apply for enforcement to the Intermediate People's Court of the place where the respondent has its domicile or where the property is located.

If an arbitration award is ruled by the People's Court not to be enforced, the parties may apply for arbitration again pursuant to a written arbitration agreement reached between them, or may institute an action before the People's Court.

Pursuant to international treaties concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China, or in accordance with the principle of reciprocity, the People's Court and a foreign court may request each other to serve documents, investigate and collect evidence, and carry out other litigation acts on their behalf.
If the matters for which a foreign court requests assistance are detrimental to the sovereignty, security, or social and public interests of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall not execute them.

Requests for and provision of judicial assistance shall be carried out through the channels provided for in international treaties concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China; in the absence of such treaty relations, they shall be carried out through diplomatic channels.
An embassy or consulate of a foreign country in the People's Republic of China may serve documents and investigate and collect evidence on its nationals, provided that the laws of the People's Republic of China are not violated and no compulsory measures are taken.
Except as provided for in the preceding paragraph, no foreign organ or individual shall serve documents or investigate and collect evidence within the territory of the People's Republic of China without the permission of the competent authorities of the People's Republic of China.

A request letter submitted by a foreign court to the People's Court for judicial assistance and the documents attached thereto shall be accompanied by a Chinese translation or a version in another language as prescribed by an international treaty.
A request letter submitted by the People's Court to a foreign court for judicial assistance and the documents attached thereto shall be accompanied by a translation in the language of that country or a version in another language as prescribed by an international treaty.

When providing judicial assistance, the People's Court shall proceed in accordance with the procedures prescribed by the laws of the People's Republic of China. If a foreign court requests that a special method be used, it may also be carried out in the special method requested, provided that the special method requested does not violate the laws of the People's Republic of China.

If, with respect to a legally effective judgment or ruling made by the People's Court, the person subject to enforcement or its property is not within the territory of the People's Republic of China, and a party requests enforcement, the party may directly apply to a competent foreign court for recognition and enforcement, or the People's Court may request the foreign court for recognition and enforcement in accordance with the provisions of international treaties concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China, or in accordance with the principle of reciprocity.
If a legally effective arbitration award is made in accordance with law within the territory of the People's Republic of China, and a party requests enforcement, and the person subject to enforcement or its property is not within the territory of the People's Republic of China, the party may directly apply to a competent foreign court for recognition and enforcement.

If a legally effective judgment or ruling made by a foreign court requires recognition and enforcement by the People's Court, a party may directly apply to a competent Intermediate People's Court for recognition and enforcement, or the foreign court may request the People's Court for recognition and enforcement in accordance with the provisions of international treaties concluded or acceded to by that country and the People's Republic of China, or in accordance with the principle of reciprocity.

After examining a legally effective judgment or ruling made by a foreign court for which recognition and enforcement is applied for or requested, the People's Court, in accordance with international treaties concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China, or in accordance with the principle of reciprocity, shall rule to recognize its validity if it considers that the judgment or ruling does not violate the fundamental principles of the laws of the People's Republic of China and does not harm national sovereignty, security, or social and public interests; if enforcement is required, the People's Court shall issue an enforcement order and enforce it in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Law.

If a party applies to the People's Court for recognition and enforcement of a legally effective judgment or ruling made by a foreign court, and the dispute involved in such judgment or ruling is the same as the dispute being adjudicated by the People's Court, the People's Court may order suspension of the action.
If a legally effective judgment or ruling made by a foreign court does not meet the conditions for recognition provided for in this Law, the People's Court shall rule not to recognize and enforce it, and shall resume the action that has been suspended; if it meets the conditions for recognition provided for in this Law, the People's Court shall rule to recognize its validity; if enforcement is required, the People's Court shall issue an enforcement order and enforce it in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Law; with respect to the action that has been suspended, the People's Court shall rule to dismiss the prosecution.

If a party is dissatisfied with a ruling on recognition and enforcement or on non-recognition and non-enforcement, it may apply for reconsideration to the People's Court at the next higher level within ten days from the date of service of the ruling.

If a legally effective arbitration award made outside the territory of the People's Republic of China requires recognition and enforcement by the People's Court, a party may directly apply to the Intermediate People's Court of the place where the person subject to enforcement has its domicile or where its property is located. If the domicile of the person subject to enforcement or its property is not within the territory of the People's Republic of China, the party may apply to the Intermediate People's Court of the place where the applicant has its domicile or of the place that has an appropriate connection with the dispute in the award. The People's Court shall handle the matter in accordance with international treaties concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China, or in accordance with the principle of reciprocity.

Civil actions involving foreign states shall be governed by the legal provisions of the People's Republic of China on foreign state immunity; where there are no such provisions in the relevant laws, this Law shall apply.
This Law shall come into force as of the date of its promulgation, and the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation) shall be abolished simultaneously.
